arxiv-2008-08985.title: Fair and consistent prize allocation in competitions Thanks: b.dietzenbacher@maastrichtuniversity.nl — Department of Quantitative Economics, Maastricht University, Maastricht, The Netherlands — http://orcid.org/0000-0002-8023-0273 akondratev@hse.ru — corresponding author — HSE University, Internatio
arxiv-2008-08985.creator: Bas J. Dietzenbacher, Aleksei Y. Kondratev
arxiv-2008-08985.description: Abstract . Given the final ranking of a competition, how should the total prize endowment be allocated among the competitors? We study consistent prize allocation rules satisfying elementary solidarity and fairness principles. In particular, we axiomatically characterize several families of rules satisfying anonymity, order preservation, and endowment monotonicity, which all fall between the Equal Division rule and the Winner-Takes-All rule.

arxiv-2211-00619.title: Asymmetric Hashing for Fast Ranking via Neural Network Measures
arxiv-2211-00619.description: Abstract Fast item ranking is an important task in recommender systems. In previous works, graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) approaches have demonstrated good performance on item ranking tasks with generic searching/matching measures (including complex measures such as neural network measures).

arxiv-2307-07140.creator: Shuyu Tan, Quentin A. Parker, Albert A. Zijlstra, Andreas Ritter, Bryan Rees
arxiv-2307-07140.description: Abstract We report observations of a remarkable major axes alignment nearly parallel to the Galactic plane of 5 σ \sigma significance for a subset of bulge “planetary nebulae” (PNe) that host, or are inferred to host, short period binaries. Nearly all are bipolar.

arxiv-2311-05363.title: Beyond the training set: an intuitive method for detecting distribution shift in model-based optimization
arxiv-2311-05363.creator: Farhan Damani, David H. Brookes, Theodore Sternlieb, Cameron Webster, Stephen Malina, Rishi Jajoo, Kathy Lin, Sam Sinai
arxiv-2311-05363.description: Abstract Model-based optimization (MBO) is increasingly applied to design problems in science and engineering. A common scenario involves using a fixed training set to train models, with the goal of designing new samples that outperform those present in the training data. A major challenge in this setting is distribution shift, where the distributions of training and designed samples are different.

pmc-11459591.description: Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a rare immune-mediated disease affecting multiple organs and tissues. There is often the presence of elevated serum Ig4 subtype with histological evidence of lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, fibrosis, and phlebitis. The mainstay of treatment is steroid therapy.

pmc-12581455.title: Inadvertent insertion of a subclavian central venous catheter into the pulmonary artery through a Blalock-Taussig shunt: a rare complication of a common procedure
pmc-12581455.creator: Mehdi Ghaderian, Mohadeseh Ghasemi
pmc-12581455.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Central venous catheter (CVC) insertion is a common procedure providing direct access to the central venous system. Potential mechanical, infectious, and embolic complications could occur. Malpositioning into the pulmonary artery is a very rare complication. A modified Blalock-Taussig shunt (MBTS), anatomically positioned between the subclavian and the pulmonary arteries and adjacent to the right internal jugular vein, is the most common procedure performed in children with complex congenital heart disease (CHD) to enhance pulmonary artery blood flow.

pmc-12655907.title: First Detection of Sclerotinia nivalis on Carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) in Russia and Comparative Pathogenicity of Sclerotinia Isolates on Carrot
pmc-12655907.creator: Viktoriya V Medvedeva, Rashit I Tarakanov, Peter V Evseev, Evgenii S Mazurin, Svetlana I Chebanenko, Olga O Beloshapkina, Fevzi S-U Dzhalilov, Sokrat G Monakhos, Giovanni Mian, Luca Iseppi
pmc-12655907.description: White mold of carrot is mainly caused by Sclerotinia sclerotiorum, while Sclerotinia nivalis is rarely reported. This study provides the first molecular confirmation of S. nivalis on carrot in Russia, expanding knowledge of its global distribution. rDNA-ITS sequencing (100% identity with reference strains) and phylogenetic analyses confirmed the isolate as S. nivalis.

pmc-12749479.title: Geochemistry and detrital zircon U–Pb–Hf isotopic data reveal the provenance and tectonic setting of the Xujiahe Formation
pmc-12749479.creator: Fenquan Xie, Wenzhou Xiao, Mabrouk Sami, Ioan V Sanislav, Lu Han, Yifang Wang, Suhail S Alhejji
pmc-12749479.description: The depositional age, provenance and tectonic setting of the Xujiahe Formation have been studied, but remain intensely debated. In this study, we focus on the second segment of the Xujiahe Formation (T3x2) as a research object. Several sandstone samples from three sections were collected for stratigraphic, geochemical and detrital zircon analyses.

pmc-12831239.title: Prevalence of pulp stones in patients with cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12831239.creator: Merve Gökyar, Yeliz Güneş, Hesna Sazak Öveçoğlu
pmc-12831239.description: BackgroundThis retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to assess the prevalence of pulp stones in individuals diagnosed with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and/or type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) using digital panoramic radiographs. Additionally, the study investigated the potential association between these systemic conditions and the presence of pulp calcifications.

pmc-13327665.title: The Latest Global Stroke Fact Sheet 1990–2023: Global Burden of Disease Study
pmc-13327665.creator: Valery L. Feigin, Victor Volovici, Michael Brainin, Bo Norrving, Sheila O. Martins, Greg A. Roth
pmc-13327665.description: BackgroundStroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide despite substantial reductions in age-standardized rates over recent decades. Updated and comprehensive assessments of global stroke burden are essential to inform prevention strategies, health-system planning, and policy responses, particularly in the context of widening inequities between regions and the emergence of new environmental and metabolic risk factors.

pmc-13591864.creator: Xujie Duan, Wenjing Lan, Rui Liu, Pei Zhang, Sixu Chen, Yufei Zhang, Liang Zhang, Huiping Li, Shuying Liu
pmc-13591864.description: BackgroundJaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) causes ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA), and its pathogenesis is primarily mediated by the viral envelope (Env) protein. However, the detailed oncogenic mechanisms underlying JSRV infection remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to characterize JSRV Env-induced alterations in human bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B (cells).ResultsBEAS-2B cells transfected with the pcDNA4.
